reason: The text shows the people of Israel (כל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל) gathering to David in Hebron and expressing strong support: 'Behold, we are your bone and flesh' (הִנֵּה עַצְמְךָ וּֽבְשָׂרְךָ אֲנָֽחְנוּ). They make a covenant with him and anoint him as king according to God's word. The text explicitly states the mighty men 'strengthened themselves with him in his kingdom' (הַמִּתְחַזְּקִים עִמּוֹ בְמַלְכוּתוֹ). The only antagonism shown is from the Jebusites, who refuse David entry to Jerusalem—but they are not part of Israel and are subsequently conquered. The regular people of Israel are uniformly supportive of David as their leader.
